text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Banknotes of 500 and 1,000 litas will not be released to circulation because of their poor quality. The Bank of Lithuania had to withdraw from circulation the 10, 20 and 50 litas banknotes produced in 1991 and 1992 for the same reason.
- The Vilnius neuro surgery centre might have to halt its work in a few days because of financial problems.
- The Lithuanian government intends to impose restrictions on tobacco advertising instead of banning it.
- The second SAAB 340 B aircradt leased by Lithuanian Airlines arrives at Vilnius airport on Monday. The aircraft was leased from Sweden's SAAB Aircraft Credit AB for $60,000 per month.

- The movement of Eurosceptics was founded on Saturday. Rimantas Smetona, who was elected to head the National Democratic Movement, said that the movement might turn into a party before the parliamentary elections scheduled for the year 2000.
- Cardboard maker Medienos Plaushas intends to convert over 30 percent of its shares into global depository receipts.
- Lithuania's investment project commission has suggested that the government issue a guarantee for $202 million in credits necessary for the construction of Butinge oil terminal.
